```{r setup-child, child = "helpers/_setup.Rmd"}
```

```{r}
#| label: library
#| include: false
options(housepi.footer.warranty = TRUE)
options(housepi.footer.sample = TRUE)
library(housepi)
housepi_theme_set()
set.seed(42)
```

Certain models allow for the definition of custom group risks.
A group risk is *relative*: each parameter multiplies the baseline risk of a reference class, so it reads as the risk of one group with respect to that reference.
Such models allow for a number of group risks which can then be changed according to the modeler's choice.
We provide an example here with the heterogeneous version of the case-ascertained model.

# Format data features

Suppose our analysis wants to explore age and/or gender-based effects within a household survey.
We start by creating categorical groupings to stratify individuals based on their age, sex, etc. and then associate individual group risks.

```{r}
#| label: format-age-data

# define a model object with a subset of the ICoFs dataset
hhmodel <- sarscov2_2021_icofs |>
  dplyr::filter(house_id %in% sample(unique(house_id), 200)) |>
  new_housepi_model("case_ascertained")
```

The current loaded model allows for a number of group risks, among which the individual `"susceptibility"` (use `$help()` method to learn more).
We can define it calling `add_group_risk()`.
By default, all group risks without a definition will be treated as associated to the reference (i.e. `1`). Definitions will add a new parameter for each group, except for the reference group.
By default, the definition assumes the reference group to be the one with the largest number of counts.

```{r}
#| label: susceptibility-by-age
hhmodel |>
  # associate susceptibility group risk by column age
  add_group_risk("susceptibility", by = "age") |>
  # inspect group risk definitions
  get_group_risks()
```
To return a group risk to its default, overwrite its definition with argument `by` set to `NA`.
To drop all previous definitions, add a new one with `append = FALSE`.

# Dependencies between covariates

In the previous example we associated group risks to a single covariate in the data.
In this example we show how to provide more covariates and a custom reference.
Manually set a `reference` by providing the corresponding group factor values:

```{r}
#| label: susceptibility-by-sex-age
hhmodel |>
  # multiplicative group risks, adult female chosen as reference
  add_group_risk("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"),
                 reference = c(sex = "F", age = "adult")) |>
  # show corresponding tables with associations
  get_group_risks()
```

By default, parameters associated to each grouping are assumed independent,
i.e. the group risk is the product of two parameters, one for the feature "sex", another for "age".
In alternative, we can make the risk joint between the features:

```{r}
#| label: susceptibility-joint
hhmodel |>
  # here covariates are assumed to be joint
  add_group_risk("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"),
                 reference = c(sex = "F", age = "adult"),
                 joint = TRUE) |>
  get_group_risks()
```

# Parameters associated to risks

To perform inference of the parameters associated to each group we just need to provide options for the Bayesian Monte Carlo.
By default, group risk assumes lognormal prior (`meanlog = 0` and `sdlog = 3`) and a lognormal random-walk proposal (`"rw_log"`), following @cauchemez_household_2009.
This can be customized at the moment of the definition of the group risk similarly to parameters (see documentation).

```{r}
#| label: group-risk-parameters
# default parameter associated to group risks
hhmodel |>
  add_group_risk("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"), prefix = "") |>
  get_parameters()

# custom parameter priors associated to group risks
hhmodel |>
  add_group_risk("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"), prefix = "",
                 prior = "normal") |>
  get_parameters()

```

Note that direct definition of a parameter has the priority, even if a parameter with the same name would be generated by group risk application.

# Inference with group risks

We can proceed with the inference as shown in [Get started](housepi.html):

```{r}
#| label: final-group-risks

hhmodel <- hhmodel |>
  # load group risks from definition list
  add_group_risk(
    infectivity = "isolated",
    susceptibility = list(by = "vacc_status", reference = "unvaccinated")
  )

# show parameter definitions used for the inference
get_parameters(hhmodel)
```


```{r}
#| label: inference-group-risks
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Six trace plots displaying MCMC sampling behaviour for model parameters: alpha, beta, infectivity by isolation, and susceptibility parameters stratified by vaccination status.
#|  Multiple chains (1-3) are overlaid across iterations, showing convergence diagnostics and mixing properties of the Markov chains.

test_delay <- 8
hhmodel <- hhmodel |>
  # parameter definitions
  add_parameter(
    alpha = list(prior = "uniform", proposal = "rw_log"),
    beta = list(prior = "uniform", proposal = "rw_log"),
    gamma = list(prior = "uniform", proposal = "rw_unif", max = 5),
    hhsize_ref = 5
  ) |>
  # augmented definitions
  add_augmented(
    # public definitions
    infec_time = list(
      model = "uniform", min = start_date@D - 8, max = end_date@D
    ),
    # accessory generic definitions
    .incub_period = list(model = "gamma", mean = 3, sd = 1.4),
    .onset_time = infec_time + .incub_period,
  ) |>
  # observation model
  add_observation(
    #> symptomatic (status = 1)
    test_date = list(
      status = 1, discr = TRUE, model = "normal",
      mean = .onset_time, sd = 1, min = floor(.onset_time)
    ),
    #> asymptomatic (status = 2)
    test_date = list(
      status = 2, discr = TRUE, model = "uniform",
      loc = ceil(infec_time), min = 0, max = 8
    )
  ) |>
  # infectivity profile definitions
  add_infectivity_profile("gamma", mean = 4, sd = 1.6)

# perform inference
results <- hhmodel |>
  run_inference(progress = 4)

bayesplot::mcmc_trace(get_parameter_draws(results))
```

# Compare group risks

Finally, we propose the following approach to visualize the difference between the estimates for the susceptibility with respect to the reference group:

```{r}
#| label: compare-group-risks-plot
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Posterior estimates of relative susceptibility by age-sex groups (adult male, child female, child male) with reference to adult females.
#|  Points show mean estimates with 95% credible intervals derived from MCMC posterior distributions.
library(ggplot2)

risk_id <- "susceptibility"
prefix <- "sus_"

tmp <- get_group_risks(hhmodel) |>
  # extract reference value and create a label
  dplyr::filter(group_risk == risk_id, param_name == ".reference") |>
  dplyr::select(vacc_status)
ylabel <- sprintf("%s (Ref: %s)", risk_id,
                  paste(paste(names(tmp), tmp, sep = " "), collapse = " "))

# compare inferred susceptibility group risks
results |>
  summarise_draws() |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_starts(variable, prefix)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(get_group_risks(hhmodel) |>
                     dplyr::select(param_name, n) |>
                     dplyr::rename(variable = param_name),
                   by = "variable") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    variable = stringr::str_remove(variable, "sus_vacc_status") |> 
      stringr::str_replace_all("_", " ")
    ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = variable, y = median, label = sprintf("[%s]", n))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "black") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(nudge_x = 0.2, nudge_y = 0.1, color = "coral") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q2.5, ymax = q97.5)) +
  labs(x = "", y = ylabel)
```
